question: What is the primary purpose of a home visiting kit in community health nursing?

options.A: Transporting heavy laboratory machinery to community centers
options.B: Providing essential clinical tools for care outside the hospital
options.C: Replacing fully equipped surgical theaters in rural areas
options.D: Storing personal items for the nurse during field trips

explanation: The kit contains mobile diagnostic and treatment supplies that allow nurses to deliver direct care in homes and communities. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is the home visiting kit especially vital for healthcare delivery in rural Nigeria?

options.A: It serves as a permanent replacement for primary health care clinics
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future hospital admissions
options.C: It allows nurses to perform major surgeries inside residential homes
options.D: It brings healthcare services closer to populations far from fixed facilities

explanation: Mobile kits bridge the accessibility gap for remote or rural populations who cannot easily reach a physical health facility. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which item belongs inside the diagnostic section of a home visiting kit?
explanation: Basic diagnostic equipment like a stethoscope and blood pressure cuff are standard components used for patient assessment. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the specific function of the clean apron included in the nursing bag?

options.A: Acting as a clean blanket for newborn infants
options.B: Filtering contaminated water for drinking purposes
options.C: Serving as a sterile bandage for large open wounds
options.D: Protecting the nurse's uniform from contamination during care

explanation: The apron acts as a physical barrier between the nurse's personal clothing and the home environment to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h2)

question: How should a nurse handle the exterior of the public health bag during a home visit?

options.A: Treat the exterior as potentially contaminated
options.B: Wash the entire bag inside a washing machine
options.C: Wipe it down with hot oil before opening
options.D: Assume the outside surface is completely sterile

explanation: The outer surface of the bag is exposed to various environments and must be handled carefully to avoid transferring pathogens. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why must a nurse place a protective barrier underneath the visiting bag before opening it?

options.A: To provide a soft cushion for fragile glass equipment
options.B: To prevent direct contact between the bag and potentially dirty surfaces
options.C: To keep the bottom of the bag warm during rainy weather
options.D: To make the bag look more professional to the family

explanation: Placing a barrier like a plastic sheet stops dirt and microorganisms from the floor from contaminating the bag. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: When should the nurse perform hand hygiene during the home visit procedure?

options.A: Only after completing all tasks inside the home
options.B: When packing the bag back into the car
options.C: Immediately after placing the bag on the floor
options.D: Before touching any clean equipment inside the bag

explanation: Hand hygiene prevents the transfer of transient microorganisms from the nurse's hands to clean equipment and supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h4)

question: How are used, contaminated instruments managed during a home visit?

options.A: Placed back directly into the clean section with unused gauze
options.B: Rinsed in the family drinking water bucket and reused
options.C: Left on the client's dining table for future family use
options.D: Kept isolated in a separate compartment or designated waste bag

explanation: Isolating used items prevents them from coming into contact with and contaminating clean equipment inside the kit. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the very first practical step a nurse takes upon entering a client's home with the kit?

options.A: Greeting the family and selecting a suitable clean working area
options.B: Putting on sterile surgical gloves before touching anything
options.C: Immediately opening the bag to hand out medications
options.D: Washing all clinical instruments in the kitchen sink

explanation: Establishing rapport and finding an appropriate workspace sets the foundation for a safe and organized home visit. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why does the nurse only take out the specific equipment needed for the current procedure?

options.A: To make packing up at the end of the visit much faster
options.B: To ensure the family does not ask questions about other tools
options.C: To minimize the risk of contaminating unneeded supplies in the home environment
options.D: To prevent the bag from becoming too heavy to carry

explanation: Exposing only necessary items reduces the surface area vulnerable to accidental contamination in a non-sterile home. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h5)

question: What maintenance task must be performed routinely on medications inside the kit?

options.A: Mixing all liquid drugs together to save storage space
options.B: Exposing all tablets to direct sunlight for sterilization
options.C: Checking expiry dates and replacing expired items
options.D: Removing product labels to keep patient privacy

explanation: Regular inventory checks ensure that expired or degraded medications and supplies are never administered to clients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)

question: Why must reusable instruments be decontaminated immediately after returning from a home visit?

options.A: To comply with the personal fashion standards of the clinic
options.B: To make the metal instruments shine brighter in the sunlight
options.C: To prevent the nurse from losing equipment inside the bag
options.D: To prevent microbial growth and ensure readiness for the next patient

explanation: Prompt reprocessing ensures that infectious agents do not multiply on instruments and are not transferred during subsequent visits. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)
